title: Third Avenue 2023 package: fixed-cell actual bus travel times

design.design: Controlled before-after / difference in differences, conditional on parallel trends and no differential spillover
design.treatment: Third Avenue 2023 complete-street package: new offset bus lane, protected bicycle lane, intersection redesign and traffic calming; spring 2023 TSP is a pre-period complication
design.segment: Northbound Third Avenue E67 to E97, 1.472 miles; last block is outside E59–E96 project boundary
design.event_series: All 24 calendar months of 2023–2024; later 2024 months descriptive, not primary estimate
design.primary_control: Lexington Avenue southbound E96 to E68 on the same route/service patterns, with paired route × weekday × clock-hour weights
independent_control_sensitivity: Madison Avenue northbound E57–E95 (M1, M3 and M4 Local)
design.weights: Fixed January–June 2023 bus-trip weights; same exact endpoint IDs, route/service class, weekday and clock hour across observed months. Primary Lexington uses the treated paired cell weights. Equal weight to the six calendar months in the before-after contrast.
design.primary_outcome: Actual bus minutes per mile, also scaled to the treated 1.472-mile segment; includes intermediate bus dwell, signals and traffic. Not door-to-door, total traveler time or isolated bicycle-lane effect.
design.pretrend_checks: Monthly treated/control gap over Jan–June 2023; January–March versus April–June 2023 placebo; full control sensitivity. Six pre months give low power and cannot prove parallel trends.
design.inference: Do not treat thousands of weekday-hour source cells as independent treatment units. Report month-level sensitivity, paired-month differences and limited six-pair uncertainty; no conventional causal p-value.

qa.inference_units_note: One treated street corridor; rows/trips are not independent policy replications.

estimates.inference_warning: Intervals describe variability in six month pairs under assumptions. One treated corridor, serial correlation, pretrend violations and spillover invalidate strong causal significance claims.

summary.causal_identification_status: Not established: primary pretrend and held-out pre-period validation are poor; control sensitivity includes a sign reversal.
summary.read_this_first: This is an executed quasi-experimental attempt and a diagnostic failure to establish a clean causal effect. It supports a descriptive improvement and conditional package estimate, not a definitive bicycle-lane or all-traveler time effect.

treatment.fact: July 17, 2023 announcement: construction to begin the following week on E59–E96; offset bus lane, protected bike lane and intersection measures. Spring 2023 transit signal priority had already been installed on Third Avenue E7–E125.
December 7, 2023 completion announcement. Used conservatively to exclude all July–December 2023 from the primary before/after contrast.

Official October 2022 design, PDF pages 16–17, shows existing five vehicle travel lanes and proposed three, with protected bike and offset bus lanes. Confirms moving-lane reallocation, not only a painted bike marking.
Official project checklist explicitly includes bus lanes, protected bike lane, pedestrian islands, daylighting and signal retiming. These components cannot be separately identified by this design.

outcome.fact: MTA BM2 infers timepoint arrivals from GPS. Published actual average travel minutes include dwell, traffic signals, reliefs and disruptions. Monthly weekday/hour bins are coarse estimates, not trip-level observations. Timepoints and route distances can change.

controls.fact: DOT lists Lexington E96–E60 offset-lane enhancement as a 2019 project. Same route/service patterns are available in both directions. Opposite direction and displaced traffic remain concerns.
DOT lists a 2023 First Avenue E61–E79 bus-lane enhancement. The chosen control begins at E79 and avoids direct overlap, but upstream spillover is possible. It is not assumed completely untreated.

DOT's 2025 release describes extending existing Madison double bus lanes south from E42 to E23 and expansion of M2/M4 camera enforcement in 2025. These documented changes are outside the primary Jan–June 2024 post window. Searches of DOT 2023/2024 project pages and MTA/DOT releases found no redesign on E57–E95 during the primary window; this is not proof that no operational or construction cointervention occurred. M1 does not retain the exact timepoint across the full primary window, so matched Madison estimates use M3 and M4 Local only.

Both share spring-2023 corridor transit signal priority. They may also share construction spillover, traffic redistribution and route operations with treatment. Northern sensitivity is M101 Limited only; do not mistake it for all three routes.

later_event_series_complications.fact: 96th Street bus and intersection redesign completion was announced December 3, 2024. All latter-half-2024 event points are descriptive and outside the primary post window.

June 17, 2024 official index links the ACE expansion announcement. M15 SBS shares the First Avenue corridor; this may affect its local-bus control too. Broader enforcement changes in later 2024 are another reason not to extend the primary window opportunistically.
2025 signal changes and northern Third Avenue extension occur after the chosen primary period; do not merge later years into the same treatment.

car_data_access.limitation: Historical 2021–July2024 DOT E-ZPass data were not retrievable anonymously in this session. This is an access result, not a claim that no historical direct car-time data exist. No car travel-time effect is estimated here.
